teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji face France, Ireland and Italy in November
teams.body: Jake White's Fiji have a November block in Europe to plan around, with France, Ireland and Italy on the schedule and the Europe-based players available for those games. White picked no Europe-based players for the 34-28 win over Japan, handing out four new caps instead. Reflecting on that win, he said: "We have a tough series in Europe with France, Ireland and Italy, but the win today will give us a lot of confidence."

lead.why: The only shortlist item that gives a fresh angle on Fiji's own schedule and squad, and the rest are repeats or sevens and league stories.

teams.heading: Joe Marchant recalled as Steve Borthwick names 36-man England training squad
teams.body: Joe Marchant returns to England's frame for the first time since the 2023 World Cup, named in Steve Borthwick's 36-man training squad for the Nations Championship Tests against Australia, Japan and New Zealand. Will Joseph is rewarded for Gloucester's strong start, while uncapped Archie McParland and Kepu Tuipulotu fill the third scrum-half and third hooker spots. Chris Ashton, the former England wing, reads the group as built on Borthwick's relationships rather than form: "If we look at this training squad, it's not picked on form, is it?"

lead.why: It is a new story about England's own squad, and it sets up the autumn selection questions better than the Smith injury, which has already been covered.

teams.heading: Jeremy Ward named in France squad but will not play in November
teams.body: Jeremy Ward has been named in France's 42-man squad but will not play in November. The South African centre completes his five-year residency only in 2027, so he will train with the group yet miss the Fiji, Springboks and Argentina Tests. Eligibility is the bigger hurdle: his four Junior Springboks appearances at the 2016 U20 Championship could tie him to South Africa, and Rapport suggests France may need the route England used for Benhard Janse van Rensburg. Ward told RMC Sport: "Maybe there is an opportunity."

lead.why: It is a France squad story that is not already covered, and it concerns a named player rather than the injury reshuffle the reader has already seen.

teams.heading: Tommy and Jimmy O'Brien forced off in Leinster's win over Munster
teams.body: Tommy and Jimmy O'Brien both left Saturday's URC interpro at the Aviva Stadium injured, a concern for Andy Farrell, who named both wings in Ireland's 36-man squad for the Nations Championship. Tommy was replaced in the second half with an apparent leg injury, while Jimmy took a head knock and was off before half-time. Leinster head coach Leo Cullen said he had not seen Jimmy in the dressing room and was unsure how Tommy was, with both being checked.

lead.why: It is a new story about Ireland's own players, with both O'Brien wings injured and both named in Farrell's squad.

teams.heading: Italy are missing 12 players for next month's Nations Championship
teams.body: Italy are missing 12 players for next month's Nations Championship, a count that puts real pressure on Gonzalo Quesada's preparations before the autumn begins. The absences sit alongside the Menoncello setback: the Toulouse centre is set to miss the autumn Tests with a left-shoulder sprain, and Italy face South Africa, Argentina and Fiji before travelling to London for the Nations Championship Finals Weekend. After three summer defeats to Japan, New Zealand and Australia, depth is the question Quesada now has to answer.

lead.why: It is a new, men's XV squad story about Italy's own players, and the Menoncello injury it sits beside has already been covered in this edition series.

teams.heading: Townsend warns fringe men that breaking into Scotland's squad won't be easy
teams.body: Townsend has warned fringe players that breaking into his Scotland squad won't be easy, and the 37-man group for November's block is a tough one to crack. Jack Dempsey keeps his place despite leaving Glasgow for Japan, while Huw Jones returns after missing the July tour through injury. Scotland host New Zealand at Murrayfield before Australia and Japan, with Ollie Leatherbarrow the only uncapped name in the group.

lead.why: A new coach warning to fringe players, distinct from the squad-naming already reported.

teams.heading: Dillon Lewis rejoins Wales squad for November Tests after two-year gap
teams.body: Dragons tight-head Dillon Lewis has joined Steve Tandy's squad for the four November Tests, after two years away. The 30-year-old made four summer starts, against the Barbarians, Fiji, Argentina and South Africa, and admits he came back with doubts about whether he was still good enough. Tomas Francis being rested and Archie Griffin's toe surgery opened the door, but both are back now, so Lewis faces a battle for the tight-head berth. "I got thrown straight in with four starts, so hopefully they liked what they saw."

lead.why: It is the only NEW item in the shortlist and concerns a Wales player's return to the national squad, which is the team's own story.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards signs with Argentina as defence coach until 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Shaun Edwards, the former France and Wales assistant, has signed as Argentina's defence coach through to the 2027 World Cup in Australia, ending speculation that England's Steve Borthwick could bring him in. Edwards told Rugby World: "Argentina was the first team to offer me a contract." He will link up with the Pumas once his current England commitment ends after next Friday's match away to the USA. He admits he would like to represent England, but says the men's boss told him the staff were happy.

lead.why: A new coaching story about the Pumas' own defence coach, separate from the injury news already run.

teams.heading: Wallabies to host All Blacks at MCG in 2027 Bledisloe Test
teams.body: Australia's 2027 home season takes shape at the MCG, where the Wallabies will host the All Blacks in a Bledisloe Cup Test as part of the Rugby Championship, under a multi-year agreement between Rugby Australia and the Victorian Government. The match completes a fixture list billed as historic, with the Bledisloe reverting to a three-Test format opening on Anzac Day, and Melbourne will also stage an extra Bledisloe Test in 2029. Rugby Australia CEO Phil Waugh described the MCG as a jewel in Australia's sporting crown.

lead.why: The only shortlist item that is Australia's own men's XV news and not already covered; the two NEW items are England's Fin Smith story (already reported today) and a deaf sevens story.

teams.heading: Japan's errors in the rain cost them against Fiji, review finds
teams.body: Japan's errors in the rain did the damage in the 28-34 defeat to Fiji at the centenary Test, according to one detailed review of the match. Mistakes came in clusters once Fiji's pressure built, leaving Japan forced into difficult next plays. The reviewer picks out a retreating pass from fly-half Ryunosuke Ito, after a box kick was caught by Kazuma Ueda, which never reached full-back Takuro Matsunaga and rolled into Japan's own in-goal area. A knock-forward on the kickoff reception gave Fiji a scrum inside Japan's 22.

lead.why: The two strongest items, the Smith move and the Fiji result, were already reported on this tab, so this is the freshest men's Japan item with its own angle: why the Fiji defeat happened.

teams.heading: Rennie welcomes eight injured players back but Ardie Savea misses out
teams.body: Dave Rennie's squad for the Nations Championship tests has the look of a side recovering its depth, with eight players returning from injury. Rennie said the group brings "a lot of quality and experience", and the returnees include Jordie Barrett, Richie Mo'unga and Anton Lienert-Brown, while Ardie Savea is not in the squad. New Zealand face Scotland, Wales and England on consecutive weekends.

lead.why: It is the newest item in the shortlist, and its angle on returning injured players and Savea's absence differs from the selection story already covered.

teams.heading: Malcolm Marx's return talks leave Kitshoff and Nyakane in the dark
teams.body: Japan-based Malcolm Marx has been in conversations about a possible return home to either the Bulls or the Sharks, and those talks have left Steven Kitshoff and Trevor Nyakane 'in the dark'. The timing is awkward for a Springbok side already facing Cheslin Kolbe's absence with a broken jaw, with concerns still over Eben Etzebeth and Vusi Moyo.

lead.why: It is a new story about a Springbok's future and the squad around him, and it is not the Kolbe injury already reported.
